## ROLE SPECIFIC RULE 4. Antagonists must follow antag-specific rules, with limited impact.
### 1. As an antagonist, don't cause excessive death, damage, or destruction beyond your objectives.
- Killing many who are not a threat to you is commonly referred to as [color=indianred]"murderboning".[/color] You’re allowed to kill in self-defense when circumstances justify it, but do not kill excessively to prevent yourself from being discovered.
- You are always allowed to round remove targets who you have the objective to kill. Don’t attempt to prevent revival of players unnecessarily. Taking steps to permanently round remove many people who are not a direct threat to you is almost always excessive.
- There is exemptions to this rule, which allows you to ignore it entirely, including objectives such as "die a glorious death" (DAGD) or playing as a major antagonist, such as nuclear operatives, heretics, wizards, and space dragons.
- Pursuing a gimmick unrelated to your objectives entirely is permissible as long as this gimmick does not cause much higher levels of disruption than your objectives would allow, or lead to non-accidental round removals of non-targets without justification.
### 2. As an antagonist, don’t use your advantages to fight other antagonists.
- Solo antagonists and team antagonists are intended to cause issues for non-antagonists or the station. Antagonists are not required to exclusively cause issues, but their net impact on non-antagonists or the station should generally be negative.
- Do not cause issues for your own team as a team antagonist.
- As a solo antagonist don't attack or sabotage actions of other antagonists without proper justification, (such as accomplishing your own objectives.) This is especially bad if you fight against minor threats, but less important to consider against major threats, which are more likely to stand in the way your goals.
